title: Design contract (.gamestudio/contract.json)
description: The one-page truth of the game: fantasy, verbs, mechanics, loops, economy, progression, content, FTUE, UX, art and audio direction, monetization, live-ops, analytics targets, technical budgets, scope, risks and kill criteria. Owned by the principal agent; every other document must stay consistent with it. Only schema_version and meta.title are required so a contract can grow section by section; design-review flags empty sections.

currency.description: A currency or countable resource the player owns.

id.description: Currency id, e.g. "coins". Economy-model resources use the same ids.

kind.description: soft (earned freely, high volume), hard (scarce, earnable and purchasable), premium (purchase-only), energy (gates play time; use sparingly), event (expires with a live event), xp (progress, never spent), material (crafting or upgrade input).

sources.description: Where the currency comes from (faucets), e.g. "level win", "daily login", "IAP".

sinks.description: Where it goes (drains), e.g. "golem upgrades", "continues". A currency without a sink inflates.

cap.description: Maximum balance, or null for uncapped. Caps on energy and event currencies stop hoarding.

track.description: A progression track: a counter that grows along a curve and unlocks content at thresholds.

type.description: Track kind. Suggested: player_level, chapter, collection, character_level, mastery, battle_pass, prestige, story.

curve.description: Cost or requirement curve of the track. progression_calc.py evaluates the standard formulas.

formula.description: Curve family: linear, poly, exp, logistic, piecewise (names used by progression_calc.py), or an explicit expression in n, e.g. "100 * 1.15^(n-1)".

unlocks.description: Content unlocked along the track, in ascending order of at.

at.description: Track value at which the unlock happens (e.g. 5), or a condition string.

unlock.description: What becomes available (feature, mechanic, world, currency).

ftue_step.description: One onboarding beat. Each beat teaches by doing within max_seconds.

id.description: Step id; becomes the step parameter of the tutorial analytics event.

goal.description: What the player achieves in this beat.

teaches.description: Verb or mechanic ids (or plain concepts) this beat teaches.

max_seconds.description: Time budget for the beat; playtests flag beats that exceed it.

id.description: Product id (later mapped to store product ids).

type.description: Merchandising type. Store billing type follows: remove_ads and permanent cosmetics are non-consumable, subscription is auto-renewing, the rest are usually consumable.

price_tier.description: Reference price in USD (e.g. 4.99) or a store price-tier label. Localised prices come from the store.

contents.description: What the player receives: a resource map {"gems": 300}, a list of items, or a description.

ad_placement.description: A rewarded-ad placement: an id string or an object with details.

location.description: Screen or moment where the offer appears.

reward.description: What watching grants, e.g. {"coins": 40} or "revive with 1 heart".

cap_per_day.description: Maximum views per player per day for this placement.

risk.description: A project risk with its mitigation.
What could go wrong, stated as a cause and an effect.

mitigation.description: What we do now to reduce it, and the trigger for the fallback plan.

meta.description: Identity and positioning of the game.

logline.description: One sentence: who you are, what you do, why it is fun.

subgenre.description: Market subgenre, e.g. "merge tower defense", "match-3 with renovation meta".

session_length_target_sec.description: Intended typical session length in seconds; mobile casual usually 60-300.

analogy.description: Positioning as "X meets Y" (see skill analogy-engine), e.g. "Rush Royale meets Royal Match".

comparables.description: Reference games with what we borrow and what we change.

pillars.description: 3-5 design pillars: short, opinionated statements used to accept or reject every feature.

player_fantasy.description: The fantasy the player lives, in the second person ("You are..."). Every mechanic should serve it.

verbs.description: Player verbs; keep the core set at 1-3 for casual mobile.

mechanics.description: Mechanics: verbs bound to rules and tunable parameters.

loops.description: Loop graphs. Expect at least a core loop and a meta loop.

economy.description: Currencies and the pointer to the simulated economy model.

currencies.description: Every currency or countable resource; keep the count low (3-4 is typical for casual).

model_ref.description: Path to the economy model, e.g. ".gamestudio/economy/v1.economy.json" (economy-model.schema.json).

progression.description: Progression tracks and the difficulty model.

model.description: Curve shape and rationale, e.g. "sawtooth: 9 levels ramp then 1 hard level, period 10" (difficulty_curve.py patterns: linear, sawtooth, stepped).

target_win_rate.description: Average first-attempt win rate the curve aims for, as a ratio.

dda.description: Dynamic difficulty adjustment: false for none, or a description / object with trigger, adjustment and bounds. Must never be tied to spending.

target_count.description: Levels needed for the current scope tier.

generation.description: handmade, procedural (generator plus solver validation), or hybrid (generated then curated).

spec_ref.description: Folder or file with level specs, e.g. ".gamestudio/levels/" (level-spec.schema.json).

worlds.description: World / chapter count, or a list of world names or objects.

characters.description: Character count, or a list of character names or objects.

aha_seconds_target.description: Seconds from first launch to the first moment of real fun. Practitioner guidance treats more than about 90 s as a retention risk.

ux.description: UX plan: HUD, screens, accessibility. Free-form, detailed in the UX docs.

hud.description: HUD elements and their placement (thumb zone, safe areas).

accessibility.description: Accessibility commitments, e.g. colour-blind-safe palette, text scaling, reduced motion, haptics toggle.

art_direction.description: Visual direction summary; details live in the style bible.

style.description: Style in a few words, e.g. "chunky hand-painted 2D, soft outlines, top-down 3/4".

palette.description: Palette as hex colours ("#RRGGBB") or a verbal description string.

references.description: Reference images (paths/URLs) or games for the look.

bible_ref.description: Path to the style bible document.

audio_direction.description: Audio direction summary; details live in the audio bible.

music.description: Music direction: genre, tempo, instrumentation, adaptivity.

sfx.description: SFX direction: palette, priority rules, UI sound language.

voice.description: Voice direction, or null for no voice.

bible_ref.description: Path to the audio bible document.

monetization.description: IAP catalogue, ad rules, pass, and the ethics rules that constrain them all.

interstitial.description: Interstitial pacing, or null for none.

first_after_sec.description: No interstitial before this many seconds of cumulative play (protects the FTUE).

pass.description: Season / battle pass design, or null / false for none.

ethics.description: Binding monetization ethics rules, e.g. odds disclosure, no fake urgency, protections for minors.

cadence.description: Rhythm of events and updates, e.g. "weekend event weekly, 4-week season, content drop monthly".

events.description: Event types (names or objects with id, type, duration, reward).

analytics.description: KPI targets and the event taxonomy pointer.

kpi_targets.description: Targets the game must hit to graduate tiers. Retention and conversion are ratios (0.40 = 40%).

session_len_sec.description: Target average session length in seconds.

sessions_per_day.description: Target sessions per daily active user.

arpdau_usd.description: Target average revenue per daily active user, USD (IAP plus ads).

payer_conversion.description: Target share of users who ever pay.

taxonomy_ref.description: Path to the event taxonomy, e.g. ".gamestudio/analytics/events.taxonomy.json".

architecture.description: Architecture style. Default "sim-core+presentation": deterministic, engine-independent simulation plus a presentation layer.

deterministic.description: Whether the simulation is deterministic given a seed and input stream (needed for scripted playthroughs and replays).

gpu_class.description: Minimum GPU class, e.g. "Mali-G52 / Adreno 610 class".

perf_budgets.description: Performance budgets on the reference device tier; the perf gate compares perf reports against them.

fps_target.description: Target frame rate (30 or 60 typical; higher only with an explicit battery decision).

frame_ms_p95.description: 95th-percentile frame time budget in ms (16.6 for 60 fps, 33.3 for 30 fps).

memory_mb.description: Peak resident memory budget in MB on the reference device.

download_mb.description: Install download size budget in MB.

cold_start_sec.description: Cold start to interactive budget in seconds.

scope.description: Scope for the current tier as explicit must / should / won't lists.

must.description: Must-haves; the tier fails without them.

wont.description: Explicitly out of scope for this tier.

kill_criteria.description: Measurable conditions under which the project stops or pivots, e.g. "D1 < 0.30 after two FTUE iterations in soft launch".
